Odin × Godot

Production validation

7 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Recorded production runsCommandsControlled logging and delivery/service pause proofRetained evidence and boundsCallback allocation lifetime

The production runner uses the ordinary authored Kit and Replay exports. Each framework/target/case has a fresh output directory and separate evidence. Current runner source and pure Python checks alone establish no exported result. Actual current runs are recorded in the production report. Existing Gate B, Gate C and desktop reports remain their original scoped evidence.

Recorded production runs#

The 2026-11-02 execution used the four-body/four-asset/one-hinge authored scene, two real exported processes per pair, and scripted inputs from both seats.

Target Framework Observed seconds after both GO Final confirmed tick Sampled per-process RSS peak, bytes
macOS arm64, native Kit 1809.9187175 108600 122404864
macOS arm64, native Replay 1809.173003958 108600 128974848
Linux x86_64, translated Kit 1810.3640276289989 108600 181174272
Linux x86_64, translated Replay 1809.417124058 108600 185798656

All four pairs matched the five complete state parts byte-for-byte at the target, observed their real terminal signature ACK, exited naturally with code0, drained and fsynced intake, and returned Native/wrapper/Meter allocations and sample-owned owners to their observed baselines. Peak tracked admission was16621917 bytes, below67108864. Both300ms and3000ms service-pause cases passed on every pair; actual observed head gaps were16–17 and176–179 respectively. Kit used validated canonical recovery; Replay's short pause used bounded same-scope catchup and its deep pause used validated canonical recovery.

The shared-domain64MiB refusal/preservation/resume checks and public H128/window tests have separate records. Ten current Native whole-call streams retain all190 CPU samples: none exceeded4ms and the largest was3.572ms. The analyzer's individual normal-only/repair-only coverage labels remain INCOMPLETE; this is no combined hardware or general application CPU qualification. The older8.894ms failure is preserved with cause unknown.

These are bounded headless functional observations. RSS is outside the tracked physics quota, includes startup and teardown, and establishes no longer-horizon bound. One Linux RSS endpoint was0 during exit; it remains in the raw record and is not used as a leak diagnosis. The task container's OOM-kill counter stayed1 before/after the corrected runs; that existing count and historical peak belong to the preserved earlier failed run. No resource limit or counter was reset.

Native Linux hardware, remote CI execution, cross-target state equality, packet loss/jitter certification and manual visual/usability qualification remain outside these records. The remaining hardening cards and whole project are not complete.

Commands#

tests/box3d_production/runner/run.py defaults to writing plan.json with STAGED_ONLY and zero jobs. Tools and Native inputs are explicit absolute paths; the output must be new and outside the repository. A typical declaration is:

Shell
python3 tests/box3d_production/runner/run.py \
  --target macos-arm64 --framework kit --case functional \
  --godot /absolute/Godot --odin /absolute/odin \
  --native-library /absolute/libogb3.dylib --native-sha256 "$NATIVE_SHA256" \
  --out /absolute/new-case-output --port 42120

Add --execute only for an assigned actual run. It invokes the existing normal export helper, then runner/controller.py against the actual export record and exported executable, with --headless and no project/runtime-library override. --framework replay selects the sibling implementation. Linux uses --target linux-x86_64, explicit --execution-mode native or translated-linux-x86_64, and --toolchain-report /absolute/preflight.json. It runs inside the selected Linux userspace. Native hardware and translated functional evidence remain distinct; the runner validates actual tool hashes against the existing desktop preflight contract. No VM is started by this CLI.

Case Terminal tick Required workload Minimum observed duration Supervisor
functional 120 default; explicit 120–3600 terminal 0 180 s default
long 108600 108000 1800 s after both actual GO observations 2400 s
pause300 1200 default terminal actual stopped interval ≥300 ms 240 s default
pause3000 1200 default terminal actual stopped interval ≥3000 ms 240 s default

Short declarations accept --ticks and --timeout; pause cases also accept --pause-at (default confirmed tick 240), with at least 512 ticks of observation window plus 120 future ticks before the terminal target. The long declaration is fixed: 600 extra terminal ticks provide duration-observation headroom without lowering the required 108000 ticks or the measured 1800 seconds.

Controlled logging and delivery/service pause proof#

Every production case adds the bound, test-only pause_overlay to a new derived project through --project-overlay and --project-overlay-sha256 on the normal export helpers. Both flags are paired; ordinary exports without them retain their default flow. The overlay descriptor, source bytes, helper, copied script and derived project settings are hashed and checked before accepting the export. Overlay version 2 sets application/run/flush_stdout_on_print=true only in that derived project's [application] section, recording the prior presence/value, new value and before/after project hashes. Godot documents this setting as flushing stdout for each printed line; release defaults differ from debug. See the official ProjectSettings reference. This is a controlled logging choice, not proof of the old buffered-arrival cause. Old buffered exports/reports remain unchanged. Functional/long cases set no pause environment variables, so the overlay's process callback is inactive.

The autoload calls the existing public sample status() after normal processing. It requires actual GO and available live head/confirmed values. The Client emits its original status JSON, then immediately invokes synchronous self SIGSTOP. No Session/World frame, network advance, input or reset call occurs between that getter and the stop. The external controller verifies the exact owned PID/PGID in state T, waits the declared interval, verifies T again and resumes only that PID. A bounded Host observation window retains at most 529 live public head boundaries; the resume proof requires a recently received boundary and an actual head gap strictly greater than 8 or 128. Intake timestamps describe external observations, not an invented engine timestamp or a stale 1 Hz estimate.

Final confirmed complete-five-part equality, real authority controls and the actual terminal signature ACK establish resumed progress. Recovery is labelled canonical only when actual validated epoch/generation/serial/baseline scope metadata and its recovery count establish it. Same-scope catchup is separately labelled and also requires that final complete-state proof; a head jump alone proves neither. Missing scope/context fails the observation rather than creating a notice. There is no manual Replay Reset. These pauses test delivery/service gaps, not packet-loss/jitter certification.

Retained evidence and bounds#

The controller streams each role's stdout to a fsynced raw log, with a bounded disk SQLite index and at most 64 parsed events consumed per batch. Per-role bounds are 128 MiB raw log, 128 MiB index, 65536 events and 1 MiB per line; overflow is failure/incomplete evidence. Raw logs, index hashes, actual PIDs, argv, role environment, executable/export-record hashes and natural exit/drain facts are retained. A signal exit fails immediately even without a producer RESULT; an ordinary exit waits for queued stdout and EOF before checking RESULT. Signal exits are never labelled natural. Failure/timeout cleanup kills only owned remaining process groups and preserves their actual exit codes. Final output checks reuse the existing authored-sample five-part manifest/hash helper. No whole-run row array, outlier filtering, retry or data reconstruction is used.

SAMPLE_STATUS frontiers are live per getter. Native/Meter values are cached public observations at bounded 1 Hz, identified by native_sampled_frame and meter_sampled_frame, with null/unavailable preserved. The runner records actual admission against 67108864 bytes and component peaks without summing overlapping ledgers. OS RSS is sampled separately with first/last/min/peak and an endpoint slope; long runs require a measured trend. RSS is neither the Native quota nor a leak/cause diagnosis. Historical memory samples are not same-frame reads.

Actual ACK sources are Kit Host SAMPLE_ACK with scope verified_terminal_signature_ack/matched:true, and Replay Host SAMPLE_TAIL with stage:final_accepted/signature_match:true. The final epoch and terminal tick must match. Both natural exits, Native/wrapper/Meter zero cleanup, observed owner-baseline return, one Native image, complete final bytes, nonzero remote authority input and current bundle/helper fences are required. Exact script-module runtime copies are bound to their actual owned PIDs and source hashes; unexpected file/byte changes fail the fence.

CPU certification remains a separate Root-owned whole-call measurement. Public memory-cap and history/window fixtures are separate checks. This runner does not establish hardware CI execution, cross-target equality, a protocol change, an old-failure cause or a whole Gate/production acceptance by itself.

The source-only check is:

Shell
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m unittest discover \
  -s tests/box3d_production/runner -p test_runner.py -v

It checks planning/no-process defaults, strict parsing, bounded disk consumption, actual-status availability, ACK identity, pause/scope proof rules, overlay byte binding and Python syntax. It executes no exporter, compiler, Godot, VM or network.

Callback allocation lifetime#

Fresh owning Godot builtin returns use the existing gd_method="owned_return" contract. Callbacks borrowing converted Godot arguments use borrowed_args when their callees do not consume those references. Native callbacks also delimit their default TLS temporary arena with Odin's nested default_temp_allocator_temp_begin and default_temp_allocator_temp_end; resetting the default context does not free that arena, and free_all would invalidate a caller's outstanding temporaries. These are sample/editor callback boundaries, without a Core, Native or protocol change.

The callback lifetime fixture uses real SDK methods and primitive allocator observations added only to copied test projects. After128 warmup pairs it calls the actual status/presentation getters in two identical10000-pair batches, drops returned values, and requires exact TLS used/capacity/temp-count restoration, non-growing Godot heap on the second batch, unchanged pre-GO frontiers, checked close and Node destruction. Kit uses its interactive pre-GO close contract; a scripted Kit run correctly requires its declared target/ACK before successful close.

The preserved old Replay module failed: Godot heap grew31583859→68183859→104783859 bytes, and TLS capacity grew4→16→32MiB. Corrected Replay measured31112719 bytes at all three anchors with TLS [297,4194304,0]; corrected Kit measured31120203 bytes with TLS [13,4194304,0]. No tolerance, subtraction or relaxed cleanup assertion was used. These allocator observations are separate from Native admission and OS RSS. The original long-run signal9/OOM observations and the original scripted pre-GO fixture failure remain unchanged; the kernel victim attribution of the earlier OOM was not established.
